transcriber: second transcription of the lap's rules, written before reading the `le`, `let`, `where`, `when` and `says` of the four rules in petra/decks/aisc360.json
source: memory of ANSI/AISC 360-22 and the rows' own descriptions. No page of the standard was read, so this is weaker than a transcription from the page.

rules.says: the pull is at most 0.75 of the sum, over the bolts, of the least of a bolt's shear strength and the bearing and tearout strengths at its hole in each plate

where.why: the line of bolts is at most 38 inch long: over that, note c of Table J3.2 lowers the shear stress of an end-loaded joint, and this rule does not

rules.says: the end distance is at least the minimum edge distance of Table J3.4 for the bolt's diameter, for standard holes
the pull is at most 0.90 of the yield strength of the gross section of the weaker plate

unless.why: the pull runs along the line of bolts and shears them; the type puts no tension on a bolt
the type is a bearing-type joint, and slip resistance is asked only of a slip-critical one
the plates carry a pull along the line; the shear on their planes beside the holes is tearout and block shear, which have their own lines
the only load of the type is a pull of at least zero

left_out.why: Section J3.2 decides by what the joint is for, not by a comparison of quantities, and the type has no field that says it

as I recall Section J3.3, an oversize hole is allowed only in a slip-critical joint, so a lap with oversize holes should fail here. That is a ban on a key's name and not an inequality, and I would not write it as a made-up inequality
the task's rows hold no row for the minimum spacing of Section J3.4
the type has no field for the distance from the line of holes to a side edge
the task's rows hold no row for the maximum spacing and edge distance of Section J3.6
the net area needs the hole width of Section B4.3b and the shear lag factor of Section D3, and the task's rows hold neither
the tension path runs from the line of holes to a side edge, and the type has no field for that distance; the net areas also need Section B4.3b
the task's rows hold no row of Section J4.5
answered for standard holes only: an oversize hole adds the increment C2 of Table J3.5, which the task's rows do not hold
